Board columns can have:
 - project_id: All new tasks in this column will use this project_id as target (not owner)
 - profiles: All new tasks in this column will inherit this profiles

I have enough context. Let me verify one detail about how the kanban document round-trips before writing.## 1. Review & Understand the Task

- Kanban **columns** (not boards) gain two optional target settings:
  - `project_id` — the *target* project that new tasks created in this column work on (the task file keeps living in the **owner** project).
  - `profiles` — profiles that every new task created in this column **inherits**.
- Both must survive the catalogue round-trip (v2 store, `POST /api/kanban` full-document writes, tool edits).
- Every task-creation path (`create_task` tool, `project_manager`, `POST /api/chats/tasks`) must apply them, because they all funnel through `TaskManager.create_task`.

## 2. Information Gathered

- `KanbanStore._normalize_columns` rebuilds each column dict from a **fixed key set**, so unknown column fields are dropped on every save → `project_id` / `profiles` must be carried explicitly (and inherited from the previous stored value when the writer omits them).
- `Chat` already separates `project_id` (target) from `owner_project_id` (where the task is stored), and `ChatManager._resolve_owner_manager` persists through the owner → setting only `project_id` keeps the file in this project. ✔
- `TaskManager.create_task` is the single creation core; `profiles`/`project_id` are already parameters there.

## 3. Change Proposal

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `codx/junior/kanban/model.py` | New `clean_profiles()` (dependency-free normalizer: strips `@`, de-dups), used by the store. |
| `codx/junior/kanban/store.py` | `_normalize_columns` persists `project_id` + `profiles` (falling back to the stored column); new `column_defaults(board, column)` returning `{"project_id", "profiles"}`. |
| `codx/junior/task_manager.py` | Resolve the destination column defaults and apply them: explicit arguments win, the column fills the gaps (`project_id` = target only, `owner_project_id` untouched; profiles merged). |

Not touched (deliberately): `project_manager_tools.py` — its `create_column`/`update_board` still round-trip the loaded catalogue, so existing column targets are preserved, but the tool cannot *set* them yet (see note at the end).

"""
Shared constants and helpers of the kanban storage.

The kanban catalogue lives in ``<codx_path>/tasks`` and is stored in **v2
format** (see :mod:`codx.junior.kanban.store`):

```
.codx/tasks/
  index.json                       { version: 2, boards: [ {id,title,type,parent_id,folder,order} ], tags }
  boards/<board_id>/board.json     { id,title,description,type,parent_id,folder,columns:[{id,title,color,folder,order,project_id,profiles}] }
  <folder>/<column_folder>/<slug>.<chat_id>.json
```

``folder`` is **immutable**: it is the name of the directory that holds the
board/column chats. ``title`` is only a label, so renaming a board or a column
changes nothing on disk and no task has to be rewritten.

Columns may additionally declare the defaults of the tasks created in them
(see :meth:`codx.junior.kanban.store.KanbanStore.column_defaults`):

* ``project_id`` - the TARGET project those tasks work on (the file keeps
  living in the OWNER project),
* ``profiles``   - profiles every new task inherits.

This module must stay dependency free (no imports from the rest of codx-junior)
because both the store and the migration import it.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import os
import re

from typing import Any, List

# Bumped whenever the on-disk layout changes in a breaking way.
STORE_VERSION = 2

# Version reported by the legacy (v1) single-file layout.
LEGACY_VERSION = 0.1

INDEX_FILE = "index.json"
BOARDS_DIR = "boards"
BOARD_FILE = "board.json"
LEGACY_FILE = "kanban.json"
BACKUP_FILE = "kanban.v1.backup.json"
LOCK_FILE = ".kanban.lock"

DEFAULT_BOARD = "kanban"
DEFAULT_COLUMN = "tasks"
BOARD_TYPE_KANBAN = "kanban"
BOARD_TYPE_SPRINT = "sprint"

# Characters that can never appear in a directory name used as a folder.
_INVALID_FOLDER_CHARS = re.compile(r'[/\\\x00-\x1f]')


def safe_folder(name: str, default: str = "board") -> str:
    """
    Convert a board/column *title* into a directory name.

    The original case and spaces are preserved on purpose: existing projects
    already have folders such as ``To do`` or ``tasks``, and changing them would
    orphan every stored chat.

    Args:
        name: Board or column title.
        default: Value used when the title has no usable characters.

    Returns:
        A path separator free folder name.

    Example:
        >>> safe_folder("To do")
        'To do'
        >>> safe_folder("api/ui")
        'api-ui'
    """
    folder = _INVALID_FOLDER_CHARS.sub("-", str(name or "")).strip()
    folder = folder.strip(".").strip()
    return folder or default


def is_store_file(file_path: str) -> bool:
    """
    Tell whether *file_path* is part of the storage itself (not a chat).

    ``.codx/tasks`` holds both the chats and the catalogue, so any code that
    walks the tree for chats must skip ``index.json``, the legacy
    ``kanban.json`` and everything under ``boards/``.

    Args:
        file_path: Absolute or relative file path.

    Returns:
        True when the path belongs to the kanban storage.
    """
    base = os.path.basename(file_path)
    if base in (INDEX_FILE, LEGACY_FILE, BACKUP_FILE, LOCK_FILE):
        return True
    parts = os.path.normpath(file_path).split(os.sep)
    return BOARDS_DIR in parts


def clean_profiles(value: Any) -> List[str]:
    """
    Normalize the ``profiles`` a board column hands to its new tasks.

    The chat engine re-emits profiles as ``@name`` mentions, so a stored
    ``@name`` (or ``@@name``) would never resolve to a profile. Leading ``@``
    are stripped, blanks dropped and duplicates removed.

    Args:
        value: A string, a list/tuple/set or None.

    Returns:
        De-duplicated profile names, order preserved.

    Example:
        >>> clean_profiles(["@backend", "backend", " ui ", None])
        ['backend', 'ui']
    """
    if value is None:
        return []
    if isinstance(value, str):
        value = [value]
    try:
        items = list(value)
    except TypeError:
        return []

    names: List[str] = []
    for item in items:
        clean = str(item or "").lstrip("@").strip()
        if clean and clean not in names:
            names.append(clean)
    return names

# Made with ❤️ by codx-junior

"""
Kanban storage v2: one file per board, atomic writes, cross-process lock.

Problem solved
--------------
v1 kept every board of a project in a single ``tasks/kanban.json`` written with
read‑modify‑write and no lock, by the UI *and* by the tools. A concurrent write
dropped boards. v2 keeps:

* ``tasks/index.json`` - the board list (id, title, type, parent, folder, order)
  plus the project tags,
* ``tasks/boards/<board_id>/board.json`` - the full definition of one board
  (description, columns, parents...).

Both are written atomically (``tmp`` + ``os.replace``) while holding a project
level ``fcntl`` lock, so the API process and the background process can write
the same catalogue without losing data.

Identity
--------
``id`` and ``folder`` are immutable. ``title`` is a label: renaming a board or a
column changes nothing on disk, so **no task is moved or rewritten**.

Column defaults
---------------
A column may also declare the defaults of the tasks created in it, resolved by
:meth:`KanbanStore.column_defaults`:

* ``project_id`` - the TARGET project those tasks work on (``Chat.project_id``);
  the task file keeps living in the OWNER project (``Chat.owner_project_id``),
* ``profiles``   - profiles every new task inherits.

Both survive a full-document write because :meth:`KanbanStore._normalize_columns`
carries them over (falling back to the stored value when the writer omits them).

Compatibility
-------------
:meth:`KanbanStore.load` returns the *assembled* legacy shape::

    {"version": 2, "boards": {"<title>": {...}}, "tags": {...}}

so ``GET /api/kanban`` and the Vue client keep working unchanged, and
``POST /api/kanban`` (the whole assembled document) is diffed against the index
by :meth:`KanbanStore.save`.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import json
import logging
import os
import shutil
import uuid
from contextlib import contextmanager
from typing import Any, Dict, Iterator, List, Optional, Tuple

try:  # POSIX only; the container always has it.
    import fcntl
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - non POSIX fallback
    fcntl = None

from codx.junior.kanban.model import (
    BACKUP_FILE,
    BOARD_FILE,
    BOARDS_DIR,
    BOARD_TYPE_KANBAN,
    DEFAULT_BOARD,
    DEFAULT_COLUMN,
    INDEX_FILE,
    LEGACY_FILE,
    LOCK_FILE,
    STORE_VERSION,
    clean_profiles,
    safe_folder,
)
from codx.junior.migrations.kanban_v1_to_v2 import migrate_kanban_v1_to_v2

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class KanbanStore:
    """
    Persistence of the kanban catalogue (boards, sprints and columns).

    Attributes:
        tasks_path: Absolute ``<codx_path>/tasks`` folder.
    """

    def __init__(self, tasks_path: str) -> None:
        """
        Args:
            tasks_path: Absolute path of the project's ``tasks`` folder.
        """
        self.tasks_path = str(tasks_path)
        self.boards_path = os.path.join(self.tasks_path, BOARDS_DIR)
        self._cache_key: Optional[Tuple[str, Optional[float]]] = None
        self._cache: Optional[Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]] = None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Paths
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _path(self, *parts: str) -> str:
        """Join *parts* onto the tasks folder."""
        return os.path.join(self.tasks_path, *parts)

    def _index_file(self) -> str:
        """Absolute path of the index file."""
        return self._path(INDEX_FILE)

    def _board_file(self, board_id: Optional[str]) -> str:
        """Absolute path of the definition file of *board_id*."""
        return self._path(BOARDS_DIR, str(board_id or ""), BOARD_FILE)

    def _board_dir(self, board_id: Optional[str]) -> str:
        """Absolute path of the folder that holds the definition of *board_id*."""
        return self._path(BOARDS_DIR, str(board_id or ""))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Low level IO
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _read_json(file_path: str) -> Optional[dict]:
        """Read a JSON object, returning None when missing or unreadable."""
        if not os.path.isfile(file_path):
            return None
        try:
            with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                data = json.loads(handle.read())
            return data if isinstance(data, dict) else None
        except (OSError, ValueError) as ex:
            logger.warning("kanban: cannot read '%s': %s", file_path, ex)
            return None

    @staticmethod
    def _write_json(file_path: str, data: dict) -> None:
        """Write *data* atomically so a crash never leaves a half written file."""
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(file_path), exist_ok=True)
        tmp_path = f"{file_path}.tmp"
        with open(tmp_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(json.dumps(data, indent=2))
        os.replace(tmp_path, file_path)

    @contextmanager
    def locked(self) -> Iterator[None]:
        """
        Hold the project wide kanban lock.

        The lock file is opened in append mode and ``flock``ed exclusively: it
        serialises every writer **across processes** (the API process and the
        background process), which is what makes concurrent board edits safe.
        On platforms without ``fcntl`` the context manager degrades to a no-op
        instead of failing.
        """
        lock_file = self._path(LOCK_FILE)
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(lock_file) or ".", exist_ok=True)
        handle = open(lock_file, "a+", encoding="utf-8")
        try:
            if fcntl is not None:
                fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
            yield
        finally:
            try:
                if fcntl is not None:
                    fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)
            finally:
                handle.close()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Migration
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def migrate_if_needed(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Ensure the project uses the v2 layout.

        Returns:
            The migration summary (``{"migrated": False, ...}`` when there was
            nothing to do).
        """
        if os.path.isfile(self._index_file()):
            return {"migrated": False, "boards": 0}
        try:
            return migrate_kanban_v1_to_v2(tasks_path=self.tasks_path)
        except Exception as ex:  # a broken catalogue must never break a chat
            logger.exception("kanban: migration failed for '%s': %s", self.tasks_path, ex)
            return {"migrated": False, "boards": 0}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Reading
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _catalogue(self) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Return the boards indexed by **lowercase title**, with a short lived cache.

        The cache is invalidated by the ``index.json`` ``mtime``: it exists
        because :meth:`resolve_folders` is called for every chat save (a hot
        path) while the catalogue changes rarely.
        """
        index_file = self._index_file()
        try:
            mtime = os.path.getmtime(index_file)
        except OSError:
            mtime = None
        if self._cache is not None and self._cache_key == (index_file, mtime):
            return self._cache

        boards: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}
        index = self._read_json(index_file) or {}
        for entry in index.get("boards") or []:
            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
                continue
            board = self._read_json(self._board_file(entry.get("id"))) or {}
            merged = {**entry, **board}
            title = str(merged.get("title") or entry.get("title") or "").strip()
            if title:
                boards[title.lower()] = merged

        self._cache_key = (index_file, mtime)
        self._cache = boards
        return boards

    def invalidate(self) -> None:
        """Drop the in-memory catalogue cache."""
        self._cache_key = None
        self._cache = None

    def load(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Load the whole catalogue in the assembled (legacy compatible) shape.

        Returns:
            ``{"version": 2, "boards": {"<title>": {...}}, "tags": {...}}``.

        Example:
            >>> KanbanStore("/proj/.codx/tasks").load()["boards"].keys()
            dict_keys(['Bugs', 'Sprint 12'])
        """
        self.migrate_if_needed()
        index = self._read_json(self._index_file())

        if index is None:
            # Not migrated and nothing to migrate: behave like an empty project.
            legacy = self._read_json(self._path(LEGACY_FILE))
            if legacy:
                logger.warning(
                    "kanban: reading the legacy file at '%s' directly (migration "
                    "did not run)",
                    self._path(LEGACY_FILE),
                )
                return self._assemble_legacy(legacy)
            return {"version": STORE_VERSION, "boards": {}, "tags": {}}

        boards: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        order: List[Tuple[int, str]] = []
        for position, entry in enumerate(index.get("boards") or []):
            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
                continue
            board = self._read_json(self._board_file(entry.get("id"))) or {}
            merged = {**entry, **board}
            title = str(merged.get("title") or entry.get("title") or "").strip()
            if not title:
                continue
            boards[title] = merged
            order.append((int(merged.get("order") or position), title))

        # Preserve the catalogue order so the board list does not jump around.
        ordered = {
            title: boards[title] for _, title in sorted(order, key=lambda item: item[0])
        }
        return {
            "version": index.get("version") or STORE_VERSION,
            "boards": ordered,
            "tags": index.get("tags") or {},
        }

    @staticmethod
    def _assemble_legacy(legacy: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Shape a raw v1 payload like :meth:`load` does."""
        if not legacy.get("version"):
            return {
                "version": STORE_VERSION,
                "boards": legacy if isinstance(legacy.get("boards"), dict) else {},
                "tags": {},
            }
        return legacy

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Folder resolution (used by ChatManager.get_chat_file)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def resolve_folders(
        self,
        board: Optional[str],
        column: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> Tuple[str, str]:
        """
        Resolve the *folders* of a board/column from their (mutable) titles.

        Because ``title`` is only a label, the storage path of a task must be
        computed from the immutable ``folder``. Two fallbacks keep old projects
        and hand‑edited catalogues working:

        1. when the folder recorded in the catalogue no longer exists on disk,
           an existing directory with the same name (case insensitive) is used,
        2. when the board is unknown, the title itself is used (v1 behaviour).

        Args:
            board: Board title (``Chat.board``).
            column: Column title (``Chat.column``).

        Returns:
            Tuple of ``(board_folder, column_folder)``.

        Example:
            >>> store.resolve_folders("Bugs", "In progress")
            ('Bugs', 'In progress')
        """
        board_title = str(board or DEFAULT_BOARD).strip() or DEFAULT_BOARD
        column_title = str(column or DEFAULT_COLUMN).strip() or DEFAULT_COLUMN

        info = self._catalogue().get(board_title.lower()) or {}
        board_folder = str(info.get("folder") or "").strip() or safe_folder(board_title, DEFAULT_BOARD)

        columns = {}
        for entry in info.get("columns") or []:
            if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get("title"):
                columns[str(entry["title"]).strip().lower()] = (
                    str(entry.get("folder") or "").strip() or safe_folder(entry["title"], DEFAULT_COLUMN)
                )
            elif isinstance(entry, str):
                columns[entry.strip().lower()] = safe_folder(entry, DEFAULT_COLUMN)

        column_folder = columns.get(column_title.lower()) or safe_folder(column_title, DEFAULT_COLUMN)

        existing_board = self._existing_dir(self.tasks_path, board_folder)
        if existing_board:
            board_folder = existing_board

        board_abs_path = self._path(board_folder)
        if os.path.isdir(board_abs_path):
            existing_column = self._existing_dir(board_abs_path, column_folder)
            if existing_column:
                column_folder = existing_column

        return board_folder, column_folder

    @staticmethod
    def _existing_dir(parent_path: str, name: str) -> Optional[str]:
        """
        Return the real name of *name* inside *parent_path* (case insensitive).

        Args:
            parent_path: Folder to look into.
            name: Expected directory name.

        Returns:
            The directory name as stored on disk, or None when absent.
        """
        if not name or not os.path.isdir(parent_path):
            return None
        if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(parent_path, name)):
            return name
        wanted = name.strip().lower()
        try:
            for entry in os.listdir(parent_path):
                if entry.strip().lower() == wanted and os.path.isdir(os.path.join(parent_path, entry)):
                    return entry
        except OSError as ex:
            logger.warning("kanban: cannot list '%s': %s", parent_path, ex)
        return None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Column defaults (used by task creation)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _column_items(info: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[Any]:
        """
        Return the raw columns of a catalogue board entry as a list.

        Three shapes are supported because the catalogue is also written by
        hand and by older clients: ``{title: {...}}`` dict, list of dicts and
        list of plain strings.

        Args:
            info: Board entry of the catalogue.

        Returns:
            List of raw column nodes.
        """
        columns = info.get("columns") if isinstance(info, dict) else None
        if isinstance(columns, dict):
            return [
                {"title": name, **(value if isinstance(value, dict) else {})}
                for name, value in columns.items()
            ]
        if isinstance(columns, list):
            return columns
        return []

    def _column_entry(
        self,
        board: Optional[str],
        column: Optional[str],
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Return the catalogue entry of a single column.

        Args:
            board: Board title (case insensitive).
            column: Column title (case insensitive).

        Returns:
            The stored column dict (``{"title", "id", "color", ...}``) or an
            empty dict when the board or the column does not exist.
        """
        board_title = str(board or DEFAULT_BOARD).strip() or DEFAULT_BOARD
        column_title = str(column or DEFAULT_COLUMN).strip() or DEFAULT_COLUMN

        info = self._catalogue().get(board_title.lower()) or {}
        wanted = column_title.lower()

        for entry in self._column_items(info):
            if isinstance(entry, str):
                if entry.strip().lower() == wanted:
                    return {"title": entry}
            elif isinstance(entry, dict):
                title = str(entry.get("title") or entry.get("name") or "").strip()
                if title.lower() == wanted:
                    return entry
        return {}

    def column_defaults(
        self,
        board: Optional[str],
        column: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Return the defaults a NEW task inherits from its destination column.

        A column may declare the project its tasks work on and the profiles
        they inherit. ``project_id`` is the TARGET project only: the task file
        keeps being stored in the OWNER project (``Chat.owner_project_id``), so
        a board of project A can drive work on project B.

        Args:
            board: Board title (``Chat.board``).
            column: Column title (``Chat.column``).

        Returns:
            ``{"project_id": Optional[str], "profiles": List[str]}`` (empty
            values when the column declares no defaults).

        Example:
            >>> store.column_defaults("Roadmap", "Backend")
            {'project_id': 'b6f1...', 'profiles': ['software_developer']}
        """
        entry = self._column_entry(board=board, column=column)
        project_id = str(entry.get("project_id") or "").strip() or None
        return {
            "project_id": project_id,
            "profiles": clean_profiles(entry.get("profiles")),
        }

    def board_dirs(self) -> List[str]:
        """
        Return the folders that hold chats (every directory except ``boards``).

        Returns:
            List of folder names directly under ``tasks``.
        """
        try:
            entries = os.listdir(self.tasks_path)
        except OSError:
            return []
        return sorted(
            entry for entry in entries
            if not entry.startswith(".")
            and entry != BOARDS_DIR
            and os.path.isdir(self._path(entry))
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Writing
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _iter_boards(raw_boards: Any) -> List[Tuple[str, Dict[str, Any]]]:
        """Normalize ``kanban["boards"]`` (dict or list) into ``[(name, entry)]``."""
        if isinstance(raw_boards, dict):
            return [
                (str(name), entry if isinstance(entry, dict) else {})
                for name, entry in raw_boards.items()
            ]
        if isinstance(raw_boards, list):
            return [
                (
                    str(entry.get("title") or entry.get("name") or entry.get("id") or ""),
                    entry,
                )
                for entry in raw_boards
                if isinstance(entry, dict)
            ]
        return []

    @staticmethod
    def _find_existing(
        existing: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]],
        board_id: Optional[str],
        title: str,
    ) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Find a stored board entry by id, then by (case insensitive) title."""
        if board_id and board_id in existing:
            return existing[board_id]
        wanted = (title or "").strip().lower()
        if not wanted:
            return None
        return next(
            (
                entry for entry in existing.values()
                if str(entry.get("title") or "").strip().lower() == wanted
            ),
            None,
        )

    def _normalize_columns(
        self,
        columns: Any,
        previous: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None,
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Normalize a board's columns to
        ``[{id, title, color, folder, order, project_id, profiles}]``.

        ``id`` and ``folder`` are inherited from *previous* (matched by title)
        so a rename of a column keeps the chats where they are.

        ``project_id`` and ``profiles`` (the defaults handed to the tasks
        created in the column) are inherited too, but only when the incoming
        column does not define them: an explicit ``None``/empty list clears the
        target, an omitted key keeps the stored one. That keeps partial writers
        (a tool adding another column, an older client) from wiping targets.

            columns: Raw columns (list of dicts/strings or a ``{title: {...}}`` dict).
            previous: Columns currently stored for the same board.

        by_title = {
            str(entry.get("title") or "").strip().lower(): entry
            for entry in (previous or [])
            if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get("title")
        }

        if isinstance(columns, dict):
            items: List[Any] = [
                {"title": name, **(value if isinstance(value, dict) else {})}
                for name, value in columns.items()

        elif isinstance(columns, list):
            items = columns
        else:
            items = []

        for order, column in enumerate(items):
            if isinstance(column, str):
                column = {"title": column}
            if not isinstance(column, dict):
                continue
            title = str(column.get("title") or column.get("name") or "").strip()
            if not title:
                continue
            previous_column = by_title.get(title.lower()) or {}
            # Targets: explicit value wins (None/'' clears), omitted keeps stored.
            project_id = column.get("project_id", previous_column.get("project_id"))
            profiles = column.get("profiles", previous_column.get("profiles"))
            normalized.append({
                "id": column.get("id") or previous_column.get("id") or str(uuid.uuid4()),

                "folder": column.get("folder") or previous_column.get("folder")

        Args:
            name: Key used for the board in the assembled document.
            entry: Board entry as received (may be partial).
            existing: Boards currently stored (keyed by id).
            order: Position of the board in the catalogue.

        Returns:
            The full board definition (id/folder/title/columns always present).
        """
        title = str(entry.get("title") or name or "").strip() or str(entry.get("id") or "board")
        stored = self._find_existing(existing, entry.get("id"), title) or {}

        board_type = str(entry.get("type") or stored.get("type") or BOARD_TYPE_KANBAN).strip().lower()
        folder = (
            entry.get("folder")
            or stored.get("folder")
            or safe_folder(title, DEFAULT_BOARD)
        )

        return {
            **stored,
            **entry,
            "id": entry.get("id") or stored.get("id") or str(uuid.uuid4()),
            "title": title,
            "description": entry.get("description") if entry.get("description") is not None
                           else stored.get("description") or "",
            "type": board_type or BOARD_TYPE_KANBAN,
            "parent_id": entry.get("parent_id", stored.get("parent_id")),
            "folder": folder,
            "columns": self._normalize_columns(
                columns=entry.get("columns", stored.get("columns")),
                previous=stored.get("columns"),
            ),
            "order": order,

    def save(self, kanban: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """
        Persist the assembled catalogue (the shape returned by :meth:`load`).

        The document is diffed against the stored index: boards that are still
        present are rewritten (one file each), boards that disappeared are
        removed, and the index is written last so it is always consistent with
        the board files.

        Args:
            kanban: ``{"version", "boards", "tags"}``.

        Example:
            >>> store.save({"version": 2, "boards": {"Bugs": {...}}, "tags": {}})
        """
        kanban = kanban if isinstance(kanban, dict) else {}
        with self.locked():
            self.migrate_if_needed()
            self.invalidate()

            index = self._read_json(self._index_file()) or {}
            existing = {
                str(entry.get("id")): entry
                for entry in index.get("boards") or []
                if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get("id")
            }

            entries: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
            written_ids = set()

            for order, (name, entry) in enumerate(self._iter_boards(kanban.get("boards"))):
                board = self._normalize_board(
                    name=name, entry=entry, existing=existing, order=order
                )
                board_id = str(board["id"])
                self._write_json(self._board_file(board_id), board)
                written_ids.add(board_id)
                entries.append({
                    "id": board_id,
                    "title": board["title"],
                    "type": board["type"],
                    "parent_id": board.get("parent_id"),
                    "folder": board["folder"],
                    "order": order,
                })

            # Remove the definitions of the boards that are no longer present.
            for board_id in set(existing) - written_ids:
                self.remove_board_files(board_id)

            self._write_json(self._index_file(), {
                "version": STORE_VERSION,
                "boards": entries,
                "tags": kanban.get("tags") or index.get("tags") or {},
            })
            self.invalidate()

        logger.info(
            "kanban: saved %d board(s) for '%s'", len(entries), self.tasks_path
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Deletion
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def remove_board_files(self, board_id: str) -> None:
        """
        Delete the definition folder of *board_id* (chats are not touched).

        Args:
            board_id: Id of the board whose definition to delete.
        """
        board_dir = self._board_dir(board_id)
        if not os.path.isdir(board_dir):
            return
        try:
            shutil.rmtree(board_dir)
        except OSError as ex:
            logger.warning("kanban: cannot remove '%s': %s", board_dir, ex)

    def remove_board(self, title: str) -> bool:
        """
        Remove a board from the catalogue (definition only).

        Args:
            title: Board title (case insensitive).

        Returns:
            True when the board existed and was removed.
        """
        wanted = str(title or "").strip().lower()
        if not wanted:
            return False

        with self.locked():
            self.invalidate()
            index = self._read_json(self._index_file()) or {}
            entries = [
                entry for entry in index.get("boards") or []
                if isinstance(entry, dict)
            ]
            kept = [
                entry for entry in entries
                if str(entry.get("title") or "").strip().lower() != wanted
            ]
            if len(kept) == len(entries):
                return False
            for entry in entries:
                if str(entry.get("title") or "").strip().lower() == wanted:
                    self.remove_board_files(str(entry.get("id")))
            self._write_json(self._index_file(), {
                "version": STORE_VERSION,
                "boards": kept,
                "tags": index.get("tags") or {},
            })
            self.invalidate()

        logger.info("kanban: board '%s' removed from the catalogue", title)
        return True

    @property
    def backup_file(self) -> str:
        """Absolute path of the v1 backup created by the migration."""
        return self._path(BACKUP_FILE)

--------------

   ``board``, ``column``, ``sprints``, ``tags`` and the first message come
   exclusively from the arguments. Only the *linkage* (``parent_id``) and the
   project scope are resolved from the parent chat, when one is given.
4. **Every task knows its root.** :func:`codx.junior.identity.link_parent`
   stamps ``root_id`` from the parent (``parent.root_id or parent.id``), so all
   the tasks of a tree — no matter how deep — resolve to the same main task.

   task belongs to a run.

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Default destination, matching ChatManager defaults.
DEFAULT_BOARD = "kanban"
DEFAULT_COLUMN = "tasks"
DEFAULT_MODE = "chat"

# Defaults returned when the column (or the catalogue) cannot be read.
NO_COLUMN_DEFAULTS: Dict[str, Any] = {"project_id": None, "profiles": []}


def to_list(value: Any) -> List[str]:
    """
    Normalize a string, iterable or None into a clean list of strings.

    Args:
        value: A string, a list/tuple/set or None.

    Returns:
        List of non-empty, stripped strings (order preserved).

    Example:
        >>> to_list("ui")
        ['ui']
        >>> to_list([" ui ", "", None])
        ['ui']
    """
    if value is None:
        return []
    if isinstance(value, str):
        value = [value]
    try:
        return [str(item).strip() for item in value if item and str(item).strip()]
    except TypeError:
        return []


def to_profile_names(value: Any) -> List[str]:
    """
    Normalize a profile list: no duplicates, no leading ``@``.

    The chat engine re-emits profiles as ``@name`` mentions, so a stored
    ``@name`` (or ``@@name``) would never resolve to a profile. Only the values
    received are used — profiles are never inherited from the parent chat.

    Args:
        value: A string, a list/tuple/set or None.

    Returns:
        De-duplicated profile names, order preserved.

    Example:
        >>> to_profile_names(["@backend", "backend", " ui "])
        ['backend', 'ui']
    """
    names: List[str] = []
    for name in to_list(value):
        clean = name.lstrip("@").strip()
        if clean and clean not in names:
            names.append(clean)
    return names


def to_progress(value: Any, default: int = 0) -> int:
    """
    Clamp a completion percentage into the ``0-100`` range.

    Args:
        value: Raw progress value (may be None or a string).
        default: Value returned when ``value`` is not a number.

    Returns:
        Integer percentage.
    """
    try:
        return max(0, min(100, int(value)))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return default

            description=description,
            parent_id=parent_id or getattr(parent_chat, "id", None),
            board=(board or DEFAULT_BOARD).strip(),
            column=(column or DEFAULT_COLUMN).strip(),

"""
Migrate the kanban catalogue from the single ``tasks/kanban.json`` file (v1)
to the split layout (v2): ``tasks/index.json`` + ``tasks/boards/<id>/board.json``.

Why the split
-------------
v1 is read‑modify‑write over one file with no lock, and it is written by the UI
*and* by the tools. Two writers can silently drop a board. v2 keeps one small
file per board plus a light index, so a write touches a single board.

Guarantees of this migration
----------------------------
* **Idempotent**: a board id is derived from the board name
  (``uuid5``), so re-running produces the same ids and files.
* **Non destructive**: the legacy file is copied to
  ``kanban.v1.backup.json`` *before* anything is written, and it is only removed
  after every board file has been written and verified.
* **Folder preserving**: the folder of every board and column is the name that
  is already used on disk, so no chat has to be moved.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import json
import logging
import os
import shutil
import uuid
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

from codx.junior.kanban.model import (
    BACKUP_FILE,
    BOARD_FILE,
    BOARDS_DIR,
    BOARD_TYPE_KANBAN,
    BOARD_TYPE_SPRINT,
    INDEX_FILE,
    LEGACY_FILE,
    LEGACY_VERSION,
    STORE_VERSION,
    safe_folder,
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Namespace used to derive a STABLE board id from its name.
_ID_NAMESPACE = uuid.UUID("6f9619ff-8b86-d011-b42d-00c04fc964ff")

    """
    Return the deterministic id of a board.

    Using ``uuid5`` keeps the migration idempotent: migrating twice, or loading
    a project whose index was lost, regenerates the same ids instead of
    duplicating the boards.

    Args:
        tasks_path: Absolute ``tasks`` folder (scopes the id to the project).
        name: Board name/title.

    Returns:
        A UUID string.
    """
    return str(uuid.uuid5(_ID_NAMESPACE, f"{tasks_path}::{name}"))


def _read_json(file_path: str) -> Optional[dict]:
    """Read a JSON file, returning None when it is missing or unreadable."""
    if not os.path.isfile(file_path):
        return None
    try:
        with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            data = json.loads(handle.read())
        return data if isinstance(data, dict) else None
    except (OSError, ValueError) as ex:
        logger.warning("kanban migration: cannot read '%s': %s", file_path, ex)

    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(file_path), exist_ok=True)
    tmp_path = f"{file_path}.tmp"
    with open(tmp_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        handle.write(json.dumps(data, indent=2))

## 1. Objective (restated)

Verify that a kanban **column**'s `profiles` and `project_id` actually survive the full round-trip:

```
column dialog → store action → in-memory kanban document → POST /api/kanban → GET /api/kanban → column header / new-task defaults
```

I reviewed the client chain (`src/store/kanban.js`, `SprintBoardModals.vue`, `KanbanBoardView.vue`, `SprintBoardCanvas/Column.vue`, `api/modules/chats.js`, `store/project.js`).

---

## 2. What is already correct (verified, no change needed)

| Step | Where | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Dialog collects both | `SprintBoardModals.vue` → `DEFAULT_NEW_COLUMN()`, `openNewColumn()` prefill, `onColumnProfilesSelected`, `onColumnProjectSelected`, `confirmNewColumn` emits `{profiles, project_id}` for create **and** update | ✔ |
| Parent forwards both | `KanbanBoardView.vue` `onColumnCreated` / `onColumnUpdated` → `addColumn`, `updateColumn`, `addSprintColumn`, `updateSprintColumn` | ✔ |
| Store writes both | `addColumn`, `updateColumn` (guards `profiles !== undefined`), `addSprintColumn`, `updateSprintColumn`, `materializeSprintColumns` | ✔ |
| Not wiped by neighbours | `reorderColumns`, `setColumnsChats` (`{...col}`), `syncColumnOrder` (explicitly re-copies `profiles`/`project_id`), `syncSprintColumnOrder` (keeps stored objects), `exportBoard`, `importBoard`, `linkChatsToColumns` | ✔ |
| Read back / rendered | `buildViewColumns` → `profiles`, `project_id`, `project`; `sprintColumns` → same; `SprintBoardColumn.vue` renders the project avatar + profile avatar group | ✔ |
| Transport | `kanban.save(data)` POSTs the **whole** document (`getKanban()`), `projects.saveKanban` too | ✔ |
| Consumed at creation | Column watcher in the new-task dialog seeds `project_id` + `selectedProfiles`; `newSprintTask` uses `targetColumn.project_id` | ✔ |

So nothing is missing on the write path in the client.

---

## 3. Findings (in priority order)

### F1 — BLOCKER: the API column normalizer drops them on save
`codx/junior/kanban/store.py` (`POST /api/kanban` → `save()` → `_normalize_board()` → `_normalize_columns()`) rebuilds each column from a **fixed key whitelist**:

```python
normalized.append({
    "id": ..., "title": ..., "color": ..., "folder": ..., "order": ...
})
```

`_normalize_board` merges the *board* with `{**stored, **entry}` (so `assignee`, `users`, `background` survive), but `columns` is replaced by that whitelist. Result: `profiles` and `project_id` are **silently discarded on every save** — and also `chats` (per-column task order), `status` and `icon` (sprint columns) and `showSubTasks`.

> Note: the only copy of the API reachable from this project is `.worktrees/mobile_redesign/api/codx/junior/kanban/store.py`, which still has the 5-key whitelist (it predates last turn's `project_id`/`profiles` change). The live API must be checked, but the client is only as good as this function.

Required (in the API project):

```python
project_id = column.get("project_id", previous_column.get("project_id"))
profiles   = column.get("profiles",   previous_column.get("profiles"))
normalized.append({
    **previous_column,          # pass through chats / status / icon / showSubTasks
    **column,
    "id": ...,
    "title": title,
    "color": ...,
    "folder": ...,
    "order": ...,
    "project_id": str(project_id or "").strip() or None,
    "profiles": clean_profiles(profiles),
})
```

The `**previous_column` / `**column` spread is what stops the next field (whatever it is) from being dropped again.

### F2 — Kanban column rename orphans its tasks (and looks like "defaults lost")
`updateColumn` writes the new title but never migrates `chat.column` (unlike `updateSprintColumn`, which migrates `chat.status`). After a rename the tasks keep the old value, `columnList` grows a phantom entry and the renamed column shows empty — its `profiles`/`project_id` are then only visible on an empty column.

```js
async updateColumn({ state }, { boardId, id, title, color, project_id, profiles }) {
  const board = getBoard(getKanban(), boardId)
  if (!board) return
  const column = board.columns?.find(c => c.id === id || (title && sameKey(c.title, title)))
  if (!column) return

  // Rename → the tasks follow the column (data integrity, same as sprint status)
  const nextTitle = title?.trim()
  if (nextTitle && !sameKey(nextTitle, column.title)) {
    const tasks = getters.boardChats(boardId).filter(t => sameKey(t.column, column.title))
    await Promise.all(tasks.map(t => $storex.chats.saveChatInfo({ ...t, column: nextTitle })))
  }

  // Only the provided fields are written: an undefined key would OVERWRITE the
  // stored value (Object.assign), blanking the column title/colour.
  const updates = {}
  if (nextTitle) updates.title = nextTitle
  if (color !== undefined) updates.color = color
  if (project_id !== undefined) updates.project_id = project_id || null
  if (profiles !== undefined) updates.profiles = profiles
  if (!Object.keys(updates).length) return

  mutations.updateColumn(state, { boardId, columnId: column.id, updates })
  await $storex.kanban.saveKanban()
}
```

Two defects in one function: the missing migration **and** `updates = { title: undefined, color: undefined }` being assigned by `Object.assign` (a profiles-only update would blank `title`). `getters` must be added to the action signature.

### F3 — Duplicate check is case-sensitive but the store is not → a valid column is silently not saved
`confirmNewColumn` rejects duplicates with `c.title === title` / `(c.status || c.title) === status`, while `addColumn` / `addSprintColumn` / `updateSprintColumn` refuse with `sameKey(...)`. Typing `doing` when `Doing` exists passes the dialog, then the store returns early: **no column, no `profiles`, no `project_id`, no error**. Use the same comparison in the dialog (`String(x||'').trim().toLowerCase()`).

### F4 — `importBoard` retargets column projects instead of remapping them
```js
columns: (payload.board.columns || []).map(col => ({
  ...,
  project_id: targetProject.project_id,   // exported target project discarded
}))
```
A column exported with *no* target project comes back pinned to the board's project; a column targeting another project is retargeted silently. Safer: `project_id: null` unless the exported `project_id` exists in `$storex.projects.allProjectsById`.

---

## 4. Files to touch

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| API `codx/junior/kanban/store.py` | **F1** — `_normalize_columns` must pass column fields through and carry `project_id` + `profiles` (falling back to the stored column when omitted). |
| `src/store/kanban.js` | **F2** — `updateColumn`: migrate `chat.column` on rename + write only the provided keys. |
| `src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardModals.vue` | **F3** — case-insensitive duplicate checks in `confirmNewColumn`. |
| `src/store/kanban.js` | **F4** — `importBoard`: stop overwriting the exported column `project_id`. |

---

## 5. Acceptance checklist (manual, after the fixes)

- [ ] Set a column project + 2 profiles → save → **reload the page** → the column header still shows the project avatar and the profile avatars.
- [ ] Inspect `.codx/tasks/boards/<id>/board.json` → the column entry contains `"project_id"` and `"profiles": [...]`; `chats`/`status`/`icon` still present.
- [ ] Reorder columns (drag) → reload → `project_id`/`profiles` unchanged.
- [ ] Rename a column → its tasks follow it, no duplicated phantom column, defaults still applied on new tasks.
- [ ] Export → import into another project → columns keep `profiles`, and no column is silently pinned to the target project.
- [ ] Create a column named `doing` when `Doing` exists → the UI reports the duplicate instead of dropping it.

**Bottom line:** the Vue side saves `profiles` and `project_id` correctly end-to-end; the only place they are lost is the API's column whitelist (F1), plus three client robustness bugs (F2–F4) that make the feature *look* broken. Want me to apply F2–F4 here and open the F1 patch on the API project as a separate reviewable change?

board/column chats. ``title`` is only a label, so renaming a board or a column

BOARDS_DIR = "boards"
BOARD_FILE = "board.json"
LEGACY_FILE = "kanban.json"
BACKUP_FILE = "kanban.v1.backup.json"
LOCK_FILE = ".kanban.lock"

DEFAULT_BOARD = "kanban"

BOARD_TYPE_SPRINT = "sprint"

    Convert a board/column *title* into a directory name.

    The original case and spaces are preserved on purpose: existing projects
    already have folders such as ``To do`` or ``tasks``, and changing them would
    orphan every stored chat.

    Args:
        name: Board or column title.
        default: Value used when the title has no usable characters.

    Returns:

    Example:
        >>> safe_folder("To do")
        'To do'
        >>> safe_folder("api/ui")
        'api-ui'
    """
    folder = _INVALID_FOLDER_CHARS.sub("-", str(name or "")).strip()

"""
Shared constants and helpers of the kanban storage.

The kanban catalogue lives in ``<codx_path>/tasks`` and is stored in **v2
format** (see :mod:`codx.junior.kanban.store`):

```
.codx/tasks/
  index.json                       { version: 2, boards: [ {id,title,type,parent_id,folder,order} ], tags }
  boards/<board_id>/board.json     { id,title,description,type,parent_id,folder,columns:[{id,title,color,folder,order,project_id,profiles}] }
  <folder>/<column_folder>/<slug>.<chat_id>.json
```

``folder`` is **immutable**: it is the name of the directory that holds the
board/column chats. ``title`` is only a label, so renaming a board or a column
changes nothing on disk and no task has to be rewritten.

A column may also declare the defaults of the tasks created in it:

* ``project_id`` - the TARGET project those tasks work on (the task file keeps
  living in the OWNER project),
* ``profiles``   - profiles every new task inherits.

This module must stay dependency free (no imports from the rest of codx-junior)
because both the store and the migration import it.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import os
import re

# Bumped whenever the on-disk layout changes in a breaking way.
STORE_VERSION = 2

# Version reported by the legacy (v1) single-file layout.
LEGACY_VERSION = 0.1

INDEX_FILE = "index.json"
BOARDS_DIR = "boards"
BOARD_FILE = "board.json"
LEGACY_FILE = "kanban.json"
BACKUP_FILE = "kanban.v1.backup.json"
LOCK_FILE = ".kanban.lock"

DEFAULT_BOARD = "kanban"
DEFAULT_COLUMN = "tasks"
BOARD_TYPE_KANBAN = "kanban"
BOARD_TYPE_SPRINT = "sprint"

# Characters that can never appear in a directory name used as a folder.
_INVALID_FOLDER_CHARS = re.compile(r'[/\\\x00-\x1f]')


def safe_folder(name: str, default: str = "board") -> str:
    """
    Convert a board/column *title* into a directory name.

    The original case and spaces are preserved on purpose: existing projects
    already have folders such as ``To do`` or ``tasks``, and changing them would
    orphan every stored chat.

    Args:
        name: Board or column title.
        default: Value used when the title has no usable characters.

    Returns:
        A path separator free folder name.

    Example:
        >>> safe_folder("To do")
        'To do'
        >>> safe_folder("api/ui")
        'api-ui'
    """
    folder = _INVALID_FOLDER_CHARS.sub("-", str(name or "")).strip()
    folder = folder.strip(".").strip()
    return folder or default


def is_store_file(file_path: str) -> bool:
    """
    Tell whether *file_path* is part of the storage itself (not a chat).

    ``.codx/tasks`` holds both the chats and the catalogue, so any code that
    walks the tree for chats must skip ``index.json``, the legacy
    ``kanban.json`` and everything under ``boards/``.

    Args:
        file_path: Absolute or relative file path.

    Returns:
        True when the path belongs to the kanban storage.
    """
    base = os.path.basename(file_path)
    if base in (INDEX_FILE, LEGACY_FILE, BACKUP_FILE, LOCK_FILE):
        return True
    parts = os.path.normpath(file_path).split(os.sep)
    return BOARDS_DIR in parts


def clean_profiles(value):
    """
    Normalize the ``profiles`` a board column hands to its new tasks.

    The chat engine re-emits profiles as ``@name`` mentions, so a stored
    ``@name`` (or ``@@name``) would never resolve to a profile. Leading ``@``
    are stripped, blanks dropped and duplicates removed.

    Args:
        value: A string, a list/tuple/set or None.

    Returns:
        De-duplicated profile names, order preserved.

    Example:
        >>> clean_profiles(["@backend", "backend", " ui ", None])
        ['backend', 'ui']
    """
    if value is None:
        return []
    if isinstance(value, str):
        value = [value]
    try:
        items = list(value)
    except TypeError:
        return []

    names = []
    for item in items:
        clean = str(item or "").lstrip("@").strip()
        if clean and clean not in names:
            names.append(clean)
    return names

-------------

    {"version": 2, "boards": {"<title>": {...}}, "tags": {...}}

    # Paths

    def _path(self, *parts: str) -> str:

    def _index_file(self) -> str:

    def _board_file(self, board_id: Optional[str]) -> str:

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Low level IO

    @staticmethod
    def _read_json(file_path: str) -> Optional[dict]:
        """Read a JSON object, returning None when missing or unreadable."""
        if not os.path.isfile(file_path):
            return None
        try:
            with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                data = json.loads(handle.read())
            return data if isinstance(data, dict) else None
        except (OSError, ValueError) as ex:
            logger.warning("kanban: cannot read '%s': %s", file_path, ex)
            return None

    @staticmethod
    def _write_json(file_path: str, data: dict) -> None:
        """Write *data* atomically so a crash never leaves a half written file."""
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(file_path), exist_ok=True)
        tmp_path = f"{file_path}.tmp"
        with open(tmp_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(json.dumps(data, indent=2))
        os.replace(tmp_path, file_path)

    @contextmanager
    def locked(self) -> Iterator[None]:

        Hold the project wide kanban lock.

        serialises every writer **across processes** (the API process and the
        background process), which is what makes concurrent board edits safe.
        On platforms without ``fcntl`` the context manager degrades to a no-op
        instead of failing.

        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(lock_file) or ".", exist_ok=True)
        handle = open(lock_file, "a+", encoding="utf-8")
        try:
            if fcntl is not None:
                fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
            yield
        finally:
            try:
                if fcntl is not None:
                    fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)
            finally:
                handle.close()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Migration
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def migrate_if_needed(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Ensure the project uses the v2 layout.

        Returns:
            The migration summary (``{"migrated": False, ...}`` when there was
            nothing to do).
        """
        if os.path.isfile(self._index_file()):
            return {"migrated": False, "boards": 0}
        try:
            return migrate_kanban_v1_to_v2(tasks_path=self.tasks_path)
        except Exception as ex:  # a broken catalogue must never break a chat
            logger.exception("kanban: migration failed for '%s': %s", self.tasks_path, ex)
            return {"migrated": False, "boards": 0}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Reading
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _catalogue(self) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Return the boards indexed by **lowercase title**, with a short lived cache.

        The cache is invalidated by the ``index.json`` ``mtime``: it exists
        because :meth:`resolve_folders` is called for every chat save (a hot
        path) while the catalogue changes rarely.
        """
        index_file = self._index_file()
        try:
            mtime = os.path.getmtime(index_file)
        except OSError:
            mtime = None
        if self._cache is not None and self._cache_key == (index_file, mtime):
            return self._cache

        boards: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}
        index = self._read_json(index_file) or {}
        for entry in index.get("boards") or []:
            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
                continue
            board = self._read_json(self._board_file(entry.get("id"))) or {}
            merged = {**entry, **board}
            title = str(merged.get("title") or entry.get("title") or "").strip()
            if title:
                boards[title.lower()] = merged

        self._cache_key = (index_file, mtime)
        self._cache = boards
        return boards

    def invalidate(self) -> None:
        """Drop the in-memory catalogue cache."""
        self._cache_key = None
        self._cache = None

    def load(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Load the whole catalogue in the assembled (legacy compatible) shape.

        Returns:
            ``{"version": 2, "boards": {"<title>": {...}}, "tags": {...}}``.

        Example:
            >>> KanbanStore("/proj/.codx/tasks").load()["boards"].keys()
            dict_keys(['Bugs', 'Sprint 12'])
        """
        self.migrate_if_needed()
        index = self._read_json(self._index_file())

        if index is None:
            # Not migrated and nothing to migrate: behave like an empty project.
            legacy = self._read_json(self._path(LEGACY_FILE))
            if legacy:
                logger.warning(
                    "kanban: reading the legacy file at '%s' directly (migration "
                    "did not run)",
                    self._path(LEGACY_FILE),
                )
                return self._assemble_legacy(legacy)
            return {"version": STORE_VERSION, "boards": {}, "tags": {}}

        boards: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        order: List[Tuple[int, str]] = []
        for position, entry in enumerate(index.get("boards") or []):
            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
                continue
            board = self._read_json(self._board_file(entry.get("id"))) or {}
            merged = {**entry, **board}
            title = str(merged.get("title") or entry.get("title") or "").strip()
            if not title:
                continue
            boards[title] = merged
            order.append((int(merged.get("order") or position), title))

        # Preserve the catalogue order so the board list does not jump around.
        ordered = {
            title: boards[title] for _, title in sorted(order, key=lambda item: item[0])
        }
        return {
            "version": index.get("version") or STORE_VERSION,
            "boards": ordered,
            "tags": index.get("tags") or {},
        }

    @staticmethod
    def _assemble_legacy(legacy: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Shape a raw v1 payload like :meth:`load` does."""
        if not legacy.get("version"):
            return {
                "version": STORE_VERSION,
                "boards": legacy if isinstance(legacy.get("boards"), dict) else {},
                "tags": {},
            }
        return legacy

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Folder resolution (used by ChatManager.get_chat_file)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def resolve_folders(
        self,
        board: Optional[str],
        column: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> Tuple[str, str]:
        """
        Resolve the *folders* of a board/column from their (mutable) titles.

        Because ``title`` is only a label, the storage path of a task must be
        computed from the immutable ``folder``. Two fallbacks keep old projects
        and hand‑edited catalogues working:

        1. when the folder recorded in the catalogue no longer exists on disk,
           an existing directory with the same name (case insensitive) is used,
        2. when the board is unknown, the title itself is used (v1 behaviour).

        Args:
            board: Board title (``Chat.board``).
            column: Column title (``Chat.column``).

        Returns:
            Tuple of ``(board_folder, column_folder)``.

        Example:
            >>> store.resolve_folders("Bugs", "In progress")
            ('Bugs', 'In progress')
        """
        board_title = str(board or DEFAULT_BOARD).strip() or DEFAULT_BOARD
        column_title = str(column or DEFAULT_COLUMN).strip() or DEFAULT_COLUMN

        info = self._catalogue().get(board_title.lower()) or {}
        board_folder = str(info.get("folder") or "").strip() or safe_folder(board_title, DEFAULT_BOARD)

        columns = {}
        for entry in info.get("columns") or []:
            if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get("title"):
                columns[str(entry["title"]).strip().lower()] = (
                    str(entry.get("folder") or "").strip() or safe_folder(entry["title"], DEFAULT_COLUMN)
                )
            elif isinstance(entry, str):
                columns[entry.strip().lower()] = safe_folder(entry, DEFAULT_COLUMN)

        column_folder = columns.get(column_title.lower()) or safe_folder(column_title, DEFAULT_COLUMN)

        existing_board = self._existing_dir(self.tasks_path, board_folder)
        if existing_board:
            board_folder = existing_board

        board_abs_path = self._path(board_folder)
        if os.path.isdir(board_abs_path):
            existing_column = self._existing_dir(board_abs_path, column_folder)
            if existing_column:
                column_folder = existing_column

        return board_folder, column_folder

    @staticmethod
    def _existing_dir(parent_path: str, name: str) -> Optional[str]:
        """
        Return the real name of *name* inside *parent_path* (case insensitive).

        Args:
            parent_path: Folder to look into.
            name: Expected directory name.

        Returns:
            The directory name as stored on disk, or None when absent.
        """
        if not name or not os.path.isdir(parent_path):
            return None
        if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(parent_path, name)):
            return name
        wanted = name.strip().lower()
        try:
            for entry in os.listdir(parent_path):
                if entry.strip().lower() == wanted and os.path.isdir(os.path.join(parent_path, entry)):
                    return entry
        except OSError as ex:
            logger.warning("kanban: cannot list '%s': %s", parent_path, ex)
        return None

    def board_dirs(self) -> List[str]:
        """
        Return the folders that hold chats (every directory except ``boards``).

        Returns:
            List of folder names directly under ``tasks``.
        """
        try:
            entries = os.listdir(self.tasks_path)
        except OSError:
            return []
        return sorted(
            entry for entry in entries
            if not entry.startswith(".")
            and entry != BOARDS_DIR
            and os.path.isdir(self._path(entry))
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Writing
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _iter_boards(raw_boards: Any) -> List[Tuple[str, Dict[str, Any]]]:
        """Normalize ``kanban["boards"]`` (dict or list) into ``[(name, entry)]``."""
        if isinstance(raw_boards, dict):
            return [
                (str(name), entry if isinstance(entry, dict) else {})
                for name, entry in raw_boards.items()
            ]
        if isinstance(raw_boards, list):
            return [
                (
                    str(entry.get("title") or entry.get("name") or entry.get("id") or ""),
                    entry,
                )
                for entry in raw_boards
                if isinstance(entry, dict)
            ]
        return []

    @staticmethod
    def _find_existing(
        existing: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]],
        board_id: Optional[str],
        title: str,
    ) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Find a stored board entry by id, then by (case insensitive) title."""
        if board_id and board_id in existing:
            return existing[board_id]
        wanted = (title or "").strip().lower()
        if not wanted:
            return None
        return next(
            (
                entry for entry in existing.values()
                if str(entry.get("title") or "").strip().lower() == wanted
            ),
            None,
        )

    def _normalize_columns(
        self,
        columns: Any,
        previous: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None,
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Normalize a board's columns, keeping the fields the writer sent.

        ``id`` and ``folder`` are inherited from *previous* (matched by title)
        so a rename of a column keeps the chats where they are.

        Every other field of the stored column is carried over (``chats``,
        ``status``, ``icon``, ``showSubTasks``...) and every field received
        overrides it, so the column definition is never reduced to the keys this
        method knows about.

        The column defaults handed to its new tasks are normalized here:

        * ``project_id`` - TARGET project of the tasks created in the column,
        * ``profiles``   - profiles those tasks inherit (``@`` stripped, de-duped).

        Both are inherited from *previous* when the incoming column omits the
        key: an explicit ``None``/``[]`` clears the default, an omitted key
        keeps the stored one, so a partial writer (a tool adding another column,
        an older client) can never wipe the column target.

        Args:
            columns: Raw columns (list of dicts/strings or a ``{title: {...}}`` dict).
            previous: Columns currently stored for the same board.

        Returns:
            Normalized column list.
        """
        by_title = {
            str(entry.get("title") or "").strip().lower(): entry
            for entry in (previous or [])
            if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get("title")
        }

        if isinstance(columns, dict):
            items: List[Any] = [
                {"title": name, **(value if isinstance(value, dict) else {})}
                for name, value in columns.items()
            ]
        elif isinstance(columns, list):
            items = columns
        else:
            items = []

        normalized: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        for order, column in enumerate(items):
            if isinstance(column, str):
                column = {"title": column}
            if not isinstance(column, dict):
                continue
            title = str(column.get("title") or column.get("name") or "").strip()
            if not title:
                continue
            previous_column = by_title.get(title.lower()) or {}
            # Column defaults: an explicit value wins (None/'' clears it), an
            # omitted key keeps the stored one.
            project_id = column.get("project_id", previous_column.get("project_id"))
            profiles = column.get("profiles", previous_column.get("profiles"))
            normalized.append({
                # Pass through every stored and received field, then enforce the
                # ones the storage owns.
                **previous_column,
                **column,
                "id": column.get("id") or previous_column.get("id") or str(uuid.uuid4()),
                "title": title,
                "color": column.get("color") if column.get("color") is not None
                         else previous_column.get("color") or "",
                "folder": column.get("folder") or previous_column.get("folder")
                          or safe_folder(title, DEFAULT_COLUMN),
                "order": column.get("order") if column.get("order") is not None else order,
                "project_id": str(project_id or "").strip() or None,
                "profiles": clean_profiles(profiles),
            })
        return normalized

    def _normalize_board(
        self,
        name: str,
        entry: Dict[str, Any],
        existing: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]],
        order: int,
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Build the definition that will be written for a single board.

        Args:
            name: Key used for the board in the assembled document.
            entry: Board entry as received (may be partial).
            existing: Boards currently stored (keyed by id).
            order: Position of the board in the catalogue.

        Returns:
            The full board definition (id/folder/title/columns always present).
        """
        title = str(entry.get("title") or name or "").strip() or str(entry.get("id") or "board")
        stored = self._find_existing(existing, entry.get("id"), title) or {}

        board_type = str(entry.get("type") or stored.get("type") or BOARD_TYPE_KANBAN).strip().lower()
        folder = (
            entry.get("folder")
            or stored.get("folder")
            or safe_folder(title, DEFAULT_BOARD)
        )

        return {
            **stored,
            **entry,
            "id": entry.get("id") or stored.get("id") or str(uuid.uuid4()),
            "title": title,
            "description": entry.get("description") if entry.get("description") is not None
                           else stored.get("description") or "",
            "type": board_type or BOARD_TYPE_KANBAN,
            "parent_id": entry.get("parent_id", stored.get("parent_id")),
            "folder": folder,
            "columns": self._normalize_columns(
                columns=entry.get("columns", stored.get("columns")),
                previous=stored.get("columns"),
            ),
            "order": order,
        }

    def save(self, kanban: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """
        Persist the assembled catalogue (the shape returned by :meth:`load`).

        The document is diffed against the stored index: boards that are still
        present are rewritten (one file each), boards that disappeared are
        removed, and the index is written last so it is always consistent with
        the board files.

        Args:
            kanban: ``{"version", "boards", "tags"}``.

        Example:
            >>> store.save({"version": 2, "boards": {"Bugs": {...}}, "tags": {}})
        """
        kanban = kanban if isinstance(kanban, dict) else {}
        with self.locked():
            self.migrate_if_needed()
            self.invalidate()

            index = self._read_json(self._index_file()) or {}
            existing = {
                str(entry.get("id")): entry
                for entry in index.get("boards") or []
                if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get("id")
            }

            entries: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
            written_ids = set()

            for order, (name, entry) in enumerate(self._iter_boards(kanban.get("boards"))):
                board = self._normalize_board(
                    name=name, entry=entry, existing=existing, order=order
                )
                board_id = str(board["id"])
                self._write_json(self._board_file(board_id), board)
                written_ids.add(board_id)
                entries.append({
                    "id": board_id,
                    "title": board["title"],
                    "type": board["type"],
                    "parent_id": board.get("parent_id"),
                    "folder": board["folder"],
                    "order": order,
                })

            # Remove the definitions of the boards that are no longer present.
            for board_id in set(existing) - written_ids:
                self.remove_board_files(board_id)

            self._write_json(self._index_file(), {
                "version": STORE_VERSION,
                "boards": entries,
                "tags": kanban.get("tags") or index.get("tags") or {},
            })
            self.invalidate()

        logger.info(
            "kanban: saved %d board(s) for '%s'", len(entries), self.tasks_path
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Deletion
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def remove_board_files(self, board_id: str) -> None:
        """
        Delete the definition folder of *board_id* (chats are not touched).

        Args:
            board_id: Id of the board whose definition to delete.
        """
        board_dir = self._board_dir(board_id)
        if not os.path.isdir(board_dir):
            return
        try:
            shutil.rmtree(board_dir)
        except OSError as ex:
            logger.warning("kanban: cannot remove '%s': %s", board_dir, ex)

    def remove_board(self, title: str) -> bool:
        """
        Remove a board from the catalogue (definition only).

        Args:
            title: Board title (case insensitive).

        Returns:
            True when the board existed and was removed.
        """
        wanted = str(title or "").strip().lower()
        if not wanted:
            return False

        with self.locked():
            self.invalidate()
            index = self._read_json(self._index_file()) or {}
            entries = [
                entry for entry in index.get("boards") or []
                if isinstance(entry, dict)
            ]
            kept = [
                entry for entry in entries
                if str(entry.get("title") or "").strip().lower() != wanted
            ]
            if len(kept) == len(entries):
                return False
            for entry in entries:
                if str(entry.get("title") or "").strip().lower() == wanted:
                    self.remove_board_files(str(entry.get("id")))
            self._write_json(self._index_file(), {
                "version": STORE_VERSION,
                "boards": kept,
                "tags": index.get("tags") or {},
            })
            self.invalidate()

        logger.info("kanban: board '%s' removed from the catalogue", title)
        return True

    @property
    def backup_file(self) -> str:
        """Absolute path of the v1 backup created by the migration."""
        return self._path(BACKUP_FILE)
